chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Hafs al-Abbar, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The ghee (or clarified butter) is that which enters a stomach like it (i.e., digests easily or is pure), and indeed I dislike it for the old man.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of saman (ghee) in Shia hadith and why is it disliked for the elderly?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (as) defines *saman* (ghee) by its physical property of entering the stomach in a state similar to its entry, highlighting the Shia emphasis on natural purity and ease of digestion. His noted dislike for its consumption by the elderly reflects the practical medical wisdom of the Ahl al-Bayt, linking dietary habits to age-related physiological changes. This narration underscores the holistic approach in Shia jurisprudence where sensory qualities and bodily effects inform legal and health rulings.
